summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after a stress test was aborted due to exertional chest pain radiating to the neck, accompanied by ST-segment depression and a new reversible perfusion defect on nuclear imaging. He was started on IV heparin and Integrilin for acute coronary syndrome and underwent cardiac catheterization the following day, which revealed significant blockages in three coronary vessels. Three stents were placed, including one drug-eluting stent, with successful restoration of blood flow. Post-procedure, he remained hemodynamically stable with no rise in cardiac enzymes. A groin hematoma was noted but ruled out for pseudoaneurysm via ultrasound. He was monitored overnight, restarted on metformin, and discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy and follow up with cardiology.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
